question: Which of the following represents the Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)?
option_1: A technique for organising files and folders on a PC
option_2: A tool for optimising system resources
option_3: The use of two different credentials to verify identity
option_4: A security measure to prevent physical damage to a PC
solution_text:
The correct answer is The use of two different credentials to verify identity.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) is a security process in which a user provides two different authentication factors to verify their identity before being granted access to an account or system. (दो-कारक प्रमाणीकरण — दो अलग प्रमाण)

 

• The two factors typically come from different categories — something the user knows (a password/PIN), something the user has (an OTP, a smartphone, a security token), or something the user is (biometrics like fingerprint/face).

 

• 2FA adds an extra layer of security beyond a simple username-password login, making unauthorised access significantly harder even if the password is compromised.

 

• Common real-world examples include entering a password followed by an OTP sent to a registered mobile number, or a password followed by a fingerprint scan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• 2FA is a subset of the broader concept of Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), which may use more than two factors.

 

NOTE

 

• A technique for organising files and folders on a PC (Option 1): This describes file management, unrelated to authentication.

 

• A tool for optimising system resources (Option 2): This describes system optimisation utilities, not a security/identity-verification concept.

 

• A security measure to prevent physical damage to a PC (Option 4): Physical protection (e.g., surge protectors, casings) is unrelated to identity verification.

question: Former Karnataka CM _________ received the Padma Vibhushan at Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi for his contribution in the field of Public Affairs in 2023.
solution_text:
The correct answer is SM Krishna.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• SM Krishna, former Chief Minister of Karnataka (1999-2004) and former Union External Affairs Minister, was conferred the Padma Vibhushan — India's second-highest civilian award — for his contribution in the field of Public Affairs. (एस एम कृष्णा — पद्म विभूषण, लोक कार्य)

 

• The award was presented at a Civil Investiture Ceremony at Rashtrapati Bhavan, New Delhi, as part of the Padma Awards 2023, announced on the eve of Republic Day 2023.

 

• SM Krishna is widely credited with transforming Bengaluru into India's IT hub during his tenure as Chief Minister.

 

• He later served as the Governor of Maharashtra (2004-2008) and as Union Minister of External Affairs (2009-2012).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Padma Awards are given in three categories — Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri — in descending order of distinction, announced annually on Republic Day.

 

NOTE

 

• D Devaraj Urs (Option 1): A former Karnataka CM (1972-1980) known for major land reforms; he passed away in 1982 and was not part of the Padma Awards 2023.

 

• HD Deve Gowda (Option 2): Former Karnataka CM and former Prime Minister of India (1996-97); he was not the recipient named in this 2023 Padma Vibhushan citation.

 

• S Nijalingappa (Option 3): A former Karnataka CM (1956-1962) and later Congress President; he passed away in 2000 and was not part of the Padma Awards 2023.

question: According to the Census of India-2011, which state has the lowest sex ratio?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Haryana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India 2011, Haryana recorded the lowest sex ratio among all Indian states, at 879 females per 1000 males. (हरियाणा — सबसे कम लिंगानुपात)

 

• The national average sex ratio as per Census 2011 was 943 females per 1000 males, showing an improvement from 933 in Census 2001.

 

• Kerala recorded the highest sex ratio among states at 1084 females per 1000 males, followed by Puducherry among Union Territories overall.

 

• Haryana's skewed sex ratio has historically been linked to practices of female foeticide, prompting government schemes like 'Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao', launched from Panipat, Haryana in 2015.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The child sex ratio (0-6 years) as per Census 2011 was 919 per 1000, with Haryana again among the lowest.

 

NOTE

 

• Maharashtra (Option 1): Recorded a sex ratio of 929, better than Haryana's.

 

• Rajasthan (Option 3): Recorded a sex ratio of 928, better than Haryana's.

 

• Bihar (Option 4): Recorded a sex ratio of 918, close to the national figures but still higher than Haryana's.

question: Which view in MS PowerPoint is useful for editing or formatting a single slide at a time?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Normal view.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Normal view is the default and main editing view in MS PowerPoint, used to write and design a presentation one slide at a time. (सामान्य दृश्य — एक बार में एक स्लाइड)

 

• It displays the slide pane (the current slide, large and editable) alongside the thumbnail pane (small thumbnails of all slides) and, usually, the notes pane below.

 

• Normal view lets the user insert text, images, shapes, and other objects, and format them directly on the slide.

 

• It is the view PowerPoint opens in by default when a presentation is created or opened.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Slide Show view is used to actually run/present the presentation full-screen.

 

• Notes Page view shows a slide along with speaker notes for that slide.

 

NOTE

 

• Reading view (Option 1): Displays the presentation full-screen for reviewing it (similar to a slide show, but within a window with navigation controls), not for editing.

 

• Slide Sorter view (Option 2): Shows thumbnails of all slides together, useful for reordering or organising slides, not for detailed single-slide editing.

 

• Outline view (Option 3): Displays only the text content of all slides in outline form, useful for organising text, not for formatting a single slide's visual layout.

question: Which of the following Articles in the Constitution of India provides protection to President and Governors and Rajpramukhs?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 361.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 361 of the Constitution of India grants protection to the President and Governors (and formerly Rajpramukhs) from being answerable to any court for acts done in the exercise of their official powers and duties. (अनुच्छेद 361 — राष्ट्रपति और राज्यपाल को संरक्षण)

 

• It provides that no criminal proceedings can be instituted or continued against the President or a Governor during their term of office, in any court.

 

• It also states that no civil proceedings in which relief is claimed against the President or a Governor can be instituted during their term, without giving two months' prior notice.

 

• This immunity is meant to ensure the President and Governors can perform their constitutional functions independently, without fear of legal harassment.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 361A deals with protection of publication of proceedings of Parliament and State Legislatures.

 

• Article 361B bars a person disqualified for defection from holding a remunerative political post.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 352 (Option 2): Deals with the proclamation of National Emergency.

 

• Article 370 (Option 3): Dealt with the special status of Jammu and Kashmir (abrogated in 2019).

 

• Article 356 (Option 4): Deals with President's Rule in a state on failure of constitutional machinery.

question: As on 31 March 2024, apart from the Ministry of Home Affairs, which of the following ministries is headed by Shri Amit Shah?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Cooperation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As on 31 March 2024, Shri Amit Shah held charge of both the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Ministry of Cooperation. (सहकारिता मंत्रालय — अमित शाह)

 

• The Ministry of Cooperation was newly created in July 2021 as a separate Union Ministry to provide a dedicated administrative, legal and policy framework for strengthening the cooperative movement in India.

 

• Its stated vision is 'Sahkar Se Samriddhi' (prosperity through cooperation).

 

• Shri Amit Shah has been the first and, at that time, incumbent Union Minister of Cooperation since the ministry's creation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Shri Amit Shah is also a Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha) from Gujarat and served as BJP National President from 2014 to 2020.

 

NOTE

 

• Ministry of Minority Affairs (Option 2): Was headed by Smriti Irani as on 31 March 2024.

 

• Ministry of Coal (Option 3): Was headed by Pralhad Joshi as on 31 March 2024.

 

• Ministry of Corporate Affairs (Option 4): Was headed by Nirmala Sitharaman as on 31 March 2024.

question: Which was the first dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mamluk dynasty.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Mamluk (Slave) dynasty, founded by Qutb-ud-din Aibak in 1206 CE, was the first dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate. (मामलुक वंश / गुलाम वंश — दिल्ली सल्तनत का प्रथम वंश)

 

• Qutb-ud-din Aibak, originally a slave (Mamluk) of Muhammad of Ghor, established his rule at Delhi after Ghori's death, laying the foundation of the Sultanate.

 

• He began the construction of the Qutub Minar in Delhi, later completed by his successor Iltutmish.

 

• The Mamluk dynasty ruled from 1206 to 1290 CE, after which it was succeeded by the Khilji dynasty.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Notable Mamluk rulers include Iltutmish and Razia Sultana — the first and only woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate.

 

• The five dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate in order were: Mamluk (Slave), Khilji, Tughlaq, Sayyid, and Lodi.

 

NOTE

 

• Tughlaq dynasty (Option 1): The third dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate (1320-1414 CE), founded by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq.

 

• Khilji dynasty (Option 2): The second dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate (1290-1320 CE), founded by Jalaluddin Khilji.

 

• Lodi dynasty (Option 4): The last (fifth) dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate (1451-1526 CE), founded by Bahlul Lodi.

question: When was air transport nationalised in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1953.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Air transport in India was nationalised in 1953 through the Air Corporations Act, 1953. (1953 — वायु परिवहन का राष्ट्रीयकरण)

 

• Under this Act, the government took over the nine existing private airlines and merged them into two state-owned corporations.

 

• Air India was formed to handle international air services, while Indian Airlines was formed to handle domestic air services.

 

• The Act came into effect from 1 August 1953.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Air India (formerly Tata Airlines) was founded by JRD Tata in 1932.

 

• The Indian aviation sector was later privatised again in the 1990s following the Air Corporations (Transfer of Undertakings and Repeal) Act, 1994, ending Air India and Indian Airlines' monopoly.

 

NOTE

 

• 1950, 1951, 1952 (Options 1-3): These years pre-date the actual nationalisation, which took legal effect only with the Air Corporations Act of 1953.

question: Which of the following is one of the largest spiral galaxies?
solution_text:
The correct answer is NGC 6872.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• NGC 6872, located in the constellation Pavo, is recognised as one of the largest known spiral galaxies, spanning roughly 522,000 light-years in diameter. (एनजीसी 6872 — सबसे बड़ी सर्पिल आकाशगंगा)

 

• Its enormous size is a result of gravitational interaction with a nearby galaxy, IC 4970, which has stretched out its spiral arms.

 

• NASA's GALEX (Galaxy Evolution Explorer) ultraviolet space telescope data was used to identify and confirm its record-breaking size.

 

• For comparison, NGC 6872 is roughly five times the diameter of the Milky Way.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Galaxies are broadly classified by shape into spiral, elliptical, and irregular types (Hubble classification).

 

• The Milky Way is our home galaxy, a barred spiral galaxy of average size.

 

NOTE

 

• Milky Way (Option 2): Our home galaxy, but it is of average, not record-breaking, size among spiral galaxies.

 

• Cygnus A (Option 3): A powerful radio galaxy, classified as an elliptical galaxy, not a spiral galaxy.

 

• Maffei 1 (Option 4): A giant elliptical galaxy, not a spiral galaxy.

question: Which device is used to measure the current flow using needle deflection caused by a magnetic field force acting upon a current-carrying wire?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Galvanometer.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A Galvanometer is an electromechanical instrument used to detect and measure small electric currents, working on the principle of needle deflection caused by the magnetic field force acting on a current-carrying wire/coil. (धारामापी — विद्युत धारा मापन यंत्र)

 

• In the common moving-coil (D'Arsonval) galvanometer, a coil carrying current sits in a magnetic field; the resulting torque deflects a pointer/needle proportionally to the current.

 

• Galvanometers are highly sensitive to small currents and form the basis for constructing ammeters and voltmeters by adding appropriate shunt/series resistances.

 

• The principle relies on the motor effect — a current-carrying conductor experiences a force when placed in a magnetic field.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• A galvanometer converted to read current in amperes with a low-resistance shunt becomes an ammeter; converted with a high series resistance, it becomes a voltmeter.

 

NOTE

 

• Psophometer (Option 2): An instrument used to measure noise level (psophometric noise) in telecommunication circuits, not current via needle deflection.

 

• Potentiometer (Option 3): An instrument used to measure/compare EMF or potential difference by balancing against a known voltage, not primarily a needle-deflection current device.

 

• Ammeter (Option 4): Directly measures current in amperes; while it may use a galvanometer-type mechanism internally, the device described by the working principle in the question is fundamentally the galvanometer.

question: The Ayush Ministry has collaborated with the UK's London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine (LSHTM) to conduct a study on _________ for promoting recovery from COVID-19.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ashwagandha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's Ministry of Ayush, along with the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), collaborated with the UK's London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine (LSHTM) to conduct clinical trials studying Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) for promoting recovery from COVID-19 and Long COVID. (अश्वगंधा — कोविड-19 से रिकवरी अध्ययन)

 

• Ashwagandha is a well-known herb in Ayurveda, traditionally used as an adaptogen to reduce stress and boost immunity.

 

• The joint study aimed to scientifically evaluate whether Ashwagandha extract could help alleviate persistent fatigue and other symptoms of Long COVID.

 

• The collaboration reflects growing international interest in evidence-based validation of traditional Indian medicine (Ayush systems).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ministry of Ayush (Ayurveda, Yoga & Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy) was carved out as a separate ministry in 2014.

 

NOTE

 

• Gotu Kola (Option 1): An Ayurvedic herb known for cognitive/skin benefits, not the herb named in this specific LSHTM collaboration.

 

• Boswellia (Option 2): An Ayurvedic herb (Shallaki) used mainly for joint/anti-inflammatory purposes, not the subject of this study.

 

• Brahmi (Option 4): An Ayurvedic herb associated with memory and cognition, not the subject of this LSHTM-Ayush COVID-19 recovery study.

question: Sangeeta Shankar was awarded Sangeet Natak Akademi Award 2021 for her contribution in playing which musical instrument?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Violin.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sangeeta Shankar, a renowned Hindustani classical violinist, was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for 2021 for her contribution to instrumental music on the violin. (वायलिन — संगीता शंकर)

 

• She is a disciple (and daughter) of the eminent violinist Pandit N. Rajam, and belongs to a family with a strong legacy in Hindustani classical violin playing.

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's national academy for music, dance and drama, confers this award annually for outstanding contributions to the performing arts.

 

• Sangeeta Shankar is known for her gayaki ang (vocal style) of violin playing, a hallmark of the family tradition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (Akademi Ratna/Akademi Puraskar) is the highest Indian recognition given to practising artists in the field of performing arts.

 

NOTE

 

• Santoor (Option 1): A trapezoid-shaped Kashmiri string instrument famously played by Pandit Shivkumar Sharma, not Sangeeta Shankar's instrument.

 

• Veena (Option 2): A classical string instrument central to Carnatic music, not the instrument for which Sangeeta Shankar was honoured.

 

• Flute (Option 4): A wind instrument famously played by artists like Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia, not Sangeeta Shankar's instrument.

question: Of which of the following states/UTs is Rauf a folk dance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jammu and Kashmir.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rauf (or Roff) is a traditional folk dance of Jammu and Kashmir, performed mainly by women. (रऊफ नृत्य — जम्मू और कश्मीर)

 

• It is typically performed during spring, harvest time, and festive occasions such as Eid, with dancers forming two facing rows and swaying rhythmically.

 

• The dance is accompanied by traditional Kashmiri folk songs, often themed around nature, love, and the beauty of the Kashmir valley.

 

• Rauf is considered one of the most prominent cultural symbols of the Kashmir valley.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other folk dances of Jammu and Kashmir include Dumhal (performed by Wattal tribe men) and Hikaat.

 

NOTE

 

• Lakshadweep (Option 1): Known for folk dances like Lava and Kolkali, not Rauf.

 

• Kerala (Option 3): Known for dance forms like Kathakali, Mohiniyattam and Theyyam, not Rauf.

 

• Karnataka (Option 4): Known for folk dances like Yakshagana and Dollu Kunitha, not Rauf.

question: 'Ujjwala', a _____, was the official mascot of Khelo India – Para Games 2023.
solution_text:
The correct answer is sparrow.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Ujjwala', a sparrow, was unveiled as the official mascot of the Khelo India Para Games 2023 — the first-ever edition of the Games, held in New Delhi. (उज्ज्वला — खेलो इंडिया पैरा गेम्स 2023 की शुभंकर, गौरैया)

 

• The mascot and logo were launched by the then Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports, Shri Anurag Singh Thakur.

 

• The sparrow was chosen to symbolise strength, resilience, unity and inclusivity, reflecting the spirit of para-athletes.

 

• The Khelo India Para Games 2023 was the country's first national multi-sport event exclusively for para-athletes, held in December 2023.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Khelo India scheme was launched by the Government of India in 2018 to promote sports culture and identify talent at the grassroots level.

 

NOTE

 

• Goose, Duck, Hen (Options 1, 3, 4): None of these were the mascot; the official mascot was specifically a sparrow.

question: Which of the following exchange rates is determined by the market forces of demand and supply?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Floating exchange rate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A floating exchange rate is one where the value of a currency is allowed to be determined freely by the market forces of demand and supply for that currency in the foreign exchange market. (प्रवाहमान विनिमय दर — मांग और आपूर्ति द्वारा निर्धारित)

 

• Under this system, the central bank does not intervene to maintain a fixed value, so the exchange rate fluctuates continuously based on trade flows, capital movements, and market sentiment.

 

• India follows a managed (or 'dirty') float system, where the rupee's value is largely market-determined but the RBI intervenes occasionally to curb excessive volatility.

 

• A floating rate contrasts with pegged/fixed systems, where the government or central bank sets and defends a specific rate.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India moved from a fixed exchange rate regime to a market-determined (floating) exchange rate in 1993, following the economic reforms of 1991.

 

NOTE

 

• Soft pegged exchange rate (Option 1): The currency is pegged to another currency or basket, with some flexibility for adjustment — not purely market-determined.

 

• Fixed exchange rate (Option 3): The value is officially fixed/maintained by the government or central bank, not left to market forces.

 

• Hard pegged exchange rate (Option 4): The currency is rigidly fixed to another currency (e.g., a currency board or dollarization), with no flexibility.

question: With which of the following communities is the word 'Langar' (community kitchen) mainly associated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sikhism.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Langar, the community kitchen serving free meals to all visitors regardless of religion, caste or background, is a central institution of Sikhism. (लंगर — सिख धर्म)

 

• The tradition of Langar was started by Guru Nanak Dev, the founder of Sikhism, and was institutionalised and expanded by Guru Amar Das, the third Sikh Guru.

 

• Langar embodies the core Sikh principles of seva (selfless service), equality, and community sharing, and is served in every Gurdwara worldwide.

 

• The Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib) in Amritsar runs one of the world's largest community kitchens, serving lakhs of people daily.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Langar is served while everyone sits together on the floor (pangat), symbolising equality regardless of social status.

 

NOTE

 

• Jainism (Option 1): Emphasises non-violence (ahimsa) and asceticism, not specifically associated with the Langar tradition.

 

• Buddhism (Option 2): Centres on the teachings of the Buddha and monastic alms-giving (bhiksha), distinct from the Langar institution.

 

• Hinduism (Option 3): Has related traditions like Annadanam/Bhandara at temples, but the term 'Langar' is specifically identified with Sikh tradition.

question: Which city hosted the Asian Champions Trophy hockey tournament in 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chennai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2023 Men's Asian Champions Trophy (hockey) tournament was hosted by Chennai, Tamil Nadu, at the Mayor Radhakrishnan Stadium. (चेन्नई — एशियाई चैंपियंस ट्रॉफी हॉकी 2023)

 

• It marked the return of a major international hockey event to Chennai after about 16 years.

 

• India won the tournament, defeating Malaysia in the final held in August 2023.

 

• The Asian Champions Trophy is a hockey tournament organised by the Asian Hockey Federation, featuring the top hockey-playing nations of Asia.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• This was India's fourth title in the Asian Champions Trophy at the time.

 

NOTE

 

• Delhi, Surat, Ahmedabad (Options 1, 2, 4): None of these cities hosted the 2023 edition; the tournament was held in Chennai.

question: The district of Shivamogga that is famous for its Iron-Ore and Manganese mineral is located in which state of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Shivamogga (Shimoga) district, known for its deposits of iron ore and manganese, is located in the state of Karnataka. (शिवमोग्गा — कर्नाटक)

 

• Shivamogga lies in the Malnad region of Karnataka, in the foothills of the Western Ghats, and is often referred to as the 'Gateway to Malnad'.

 

• The district's mineral belt is part of Karnataka's broader iron-ore tracts, which also include areas like Bellary-Hospet and Chikkamagaluru (Bababudan Hills/Kudremukh).

 

• Shivamogga is also known for its rivers (notably the Tunga and Sharavathi) and the famous Jog Falls.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Karnataka's Bellary-Hospet-Sandur belt and Kudremukh are among India's major iron-ore producing regions.

 

NOTE

 

• Maharashtra (Option 2): Known for minerals like manganese in Nagpur-Bhandara belt, but Shivamogga is not located here.

 

• Rajasthan (Option 3): Known for minerals such as zinc, copper and marble, not the location of Shivamogga.

 

• Jharkhand (Option 4): A major iron-ore producing state (e.g., Singhbhum), but Shivamogga is not located here.

question: During 2015, in _________ sector, Government of India had allowed about 49% of FDI.
solution_text:
The correct answer is defence.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Government of India raised the Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) limit in the defence sector to 49% under the automatic route (with higher limits allowed via government approval), as part of reforms initiated around 2014-2015. (रक्षा क्षेत्र — 49% एफडीआई)

 

• This move was aimed at boosting domestic defence manufacturing and attracting foreign technology and investment, aligned with the 'Make in India' initiative.

 

• Previously, the FDI cap in defence was limited to 26%; raising it to 49% marked a significant liberalisation.

 

• The FDI limit in defence manufacturing was further increased to 74% (automatic route) in 2020.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• 'Make in India' was launched in September 2014 to boost domestic manufacturing across sectors, including defence.

 

NOTE

 

• Education (Option 1): 100% FDI is permitted under the automatic route in the education sector, not a 49% cap introduced in 2015.

 

• Manufacture of medical devices (Option 3): 100% FDI is permitted under the automatic route for medical devices manufacturing, not 49%.

 

• Food products (Option 4): FDI norms for food products (including through e-commerce for domestically manufactured/produced food) differ and are not the 49%-in-2015 case referenced here.

question: Community tradition is related to which of the following music streams?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hindustani Classical Music.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hindustani Classical Music, the classical musical tradition of North India, is deeply rooted in a community tradition, transmitted and nurtured through the Guru-Shishya Parampara (teacher-disciple tradition) across generations. (हिंदुस्तानी शास्त्रीय संगीत — गुरु-शिष्य परंपरा)

 

• This tradition evolved over centuries through the assimilation of diverse influences — indigenous, Persian and Central Asian — carried forward within musician communities and gharanas (schools/lineages, e.g., Gwalior, Kirana, Agra gharanas).

 

• It is characterised by distinctive ragas and talas, with knowledge and performance style passed down within closely-knit musical communities/families.

 

• This distinguishes it from purely individual or regionally-scattered folk (Lokgeet) traditions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Carnatic (Karnataka) Classical Music is the classical tradition of South India, also transmitted through guru-shishya lineages but developed distinctly from Hindustani music.

 

NOTE

 

• Karnataka Lokgeet (Option 1): Refers to the folk songs of Karnataka, an orally transmitted regional folk tradition, not the 'community tradition' classical stream referenced here.

 

• Hindustani Lokgeet (Option 3): Refers to North Indian folk songs, a folk (not classical) tradition.

 

• Karnataka Classical Music (Option 4): Refers to Carnatic classical music of South India, distinct from the Hindustani classical tradition identified as the answer.

question: As per the Census of India-2011, the density of population per km2 was ________ persons.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 382.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India 2011, the population density of India was 382 persons per square kilometre. (जनसंख्या घनत्व — 382 व्यक्ति प्रति वर्ग किमी)

 

• This was an increase from the population density of 325 persons per sq km recorded in Census 2001.

 

• Bihar recorded the highest population density among states (1,102 persons/km²), while Arunachal Pradesh recorded the lowest (17 persons/km²).

 

• Among Union Territories, Delhi recorded the highest density (11,320 persons/km²).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's total population as per Census 2011 was approximately 121.09 crore (1.21 billion).

 

NOTE

 

• 320, 345, 394 (Options 1, 3, 4): These figures do not match the actual Census 2011 population density of India, which was 382 persons per km².

question: The Central Office of the Reserve Bank of India was initially established in which present city in 1935?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kolkata.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was established on 1 April 1935 under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, with its Central Office initially set up in Calcutta (present-day Kolkata). (कोलकाता — आरबीआई का प्रारंभिक केंद्रीय कार्यालय)

 

• The Central Office was permanently shifted to Bombay (present-day Mumbai) in 1937, where it remains headquartered today.

 

• The RBI was originally established as a privately owned institution and was nationalised in 1949.

 

• The RBI serves as India's central bank, responsible for monetary policy, currency issuance, and banking regulation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The RBI's first Governor was Sir Osborne Smith; the first Indian Governor was C.D. Deshmukh.

 

NOTE

 

• Delhi (Option 1): Not the site of RBI's initial Central Office.

 

• Mumbai (Option 2): The current (post-1937) headquarters of RBI, but not where it was initially established in 1935.

 

• Chennai (Option 4): Not the site of RBI's initial Central Office.

question: Which of the following reactions leads to the formation of glucose pentaacetate from acetic anhydride?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Acetylation of glucose.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Glucose reacts with acetic anhydride through the process of acetylation, in which all five hydroxyl (-OH) groups of glucose are converted into acetate (-OCOCH3) groups, forming glucose pentaacetate. (ग्लूकोज का एसिटिलीकरण — ग्लूकोज पेंटाएसीटेट)

 

• This reaction is a key piece of evidence in organic chemistry confirming that glucose contains five -OH (hydroxyl) groups.

 

• The reaction is typically written as: Glucose + 5(CH3CO)2O → Glucose pentaacetate + 5CH3COOH.

 

• Acetylation reactions of this kind are used to identify the number of free hydroxyl groups present in a sugar molecule.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Glucose also undergoes other confirmatory reactions such as reaction with hydroxylamine (confirming the presence of a carbonyl/-CHO group) and Tollens'/Fehling's tests (confirming its reducing nature).

 

NOTE

 

• Oxidation (Option 2): Glucose undergoes oxidation with reagents like bromine water or nitric acid to form gluconic acid/saccharic acid — a different reaction, not the one forming the pentaacetate.

 

• Addition of ketone (Option 3): Glucose itself contains an aldehyde group and does not undergo formation of pentaacetate via ketone addition.

 

• Reduction (Option 4): Glucose on reduction (e.g., with H2/Ni) forms sorbitol, not glucose pentaacetate.

question: In kabaddi, when a raider touches any body part of any defender or any part of their clothing, it is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is tag.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Kabaddi, when a raider touches any part of a defender's (antagonist's) body, or any part of their clothing/accessories, using any part of their own body, it is called a 'tag'. (टैग — कबड्डी में रेडर द्वारा स्पर्श)

 

• A successful tag on one or more defenders, followed by the raider returning safely to their own court within the breath-hold (cant/'kabaddi-kabaddi') duration, earns the raiding (attacking) team points.

 

• If the raider is tagged but caught/held by defenders before returning, the defending team scores instead (this is called a 'catch').

 

• Kabaddi is played between two teams of seven players each, and involves alternating raids by one side into the opponent's half.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India has historically dominated Kabaddi at international level, including at the Asian Games, and the sport is hugely popular via the Pro Kabaddi League (PKL).

 

NOTE

 

• Catch (Option 1): Refers to the defenders successfully holding/stopping the raider from returning to their own court, resulting in points for the defending side — the opposite action.

 

• Pursuit (Option 3): Not the official kabaddi term for a raider's touch on a defender.

 

• Raid (Option 4): Refers to the overall act of a player entering the opponent's court to attempt to score, not specifically the act of touching a defender.

question: From which of the following Constitutions has the India Constitution adopted the system of 'First Past the Post'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is British Constitution.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Constitution adopted the 'First Past the Post' (FPTP) electoral system from the British Constitution, also known as the Westminster model. (ब्रिटिश संविधान — फर्स्ट पास्ट द पोस्ट प्रणाली)

 

• Under FPTP, the candidate who secures the highest number of votes in a constituency is declared the winner, regardless of whether they secure an absolute majority.

 

• This system is used for elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies in India.

 

• India borrowed several other features from the British Constitution as well, such as the parliamentary form of government, the concept of rule of law, and the office of Speaker.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's electoral system contrasts with Proportional Representation (PR), used partly for Rajya Sabha and Legislative Council elections.

 

NOTE

 

• Irish Constitution (Option 1): India borrowed the concept of Directive Principles of State Policy from Ireland, not FPTP.

 

• United States Constitution (Option 2): India borrowed features like Fundamental Rights, an independent judiciary, and the post of Vice President from the USA, not FPTP.

 

• French Constitution (Option 3): India borrowed the ideals of Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity (from the French Revolution) in the Preamble, not FPTP.
